evals.prompt: Start discovery for a new DataCoolie project with a relational database, an API, a remote file collection, and a catalog service. The owner says the supplied connection descriptions are complete and asks you to move directly to design.
evals.expected_output: Probe every declared source boundary first, keep each bounded result and status isolated, then hand only verified observations and the report to design.
expectations: Every declared source type is probed even though its description appears complete.
Probe outputs are bounded, isolated, and merged through the canonical observation contract.
Discovery creates no runtime metadata or design decision.

evals.prompt: A discovered object contains UpdatedAt, lastUpdateTime, ROW_VERSION, event_time, and orderId. Produce a compact incremental-evidence assessment without assuming that spelling or names prove semantics.
evals.expected_output: Normalize identifier styles for scratch signals, use type/key structure, leave generic event_time unconfirmed, and require semantic evidence before durable candidates.
expectations: Camel, Pascal, uppercase, and delimited identifiers are tokenized rather than requiring exact hardcoded spellings.
Signals and the compact object summary remain scratch-only and do not mutate observations.
Generic event_time and an identity on mutable data are not treated as complete change coverage.

evals.prompt: Assess two source objects. One has semantically verified creation, update, and durable tombstone columns plus an auxiliary identity. The other has no reliable change signal and unknown full-refresh cost. Make sure no object is omitted from the handoff.
evals.expected_output: Complete one object decision per object, validate the composite candidate and delete evidence, require a human decision for the unresolved object, and generate annotations plus report rows from the same scratch decisions.
expectations: The finalizer fails closed unless every observed object has exactly one valid outcome.
The composite candidate uses canonical roles and requires persistent delete evidence.
Annotations and the complete report table are derived from one scratch decision document.

evals.prompt: Catalog metadata cannot show whether a custom version token has nulls, ties, or resets. Author the smallest safe database check. The source uses an unfamiliar dialect and may contain sensitive business values.
evals.expected_output: Adapt one aggregate-oriented query to the active dialect, execute it through the bounded read-only SQL probe, and retain only the minimum scratch evidence.
expectations: Reference query purposes are adapted into one reviewed SELECT or WITH file rather than executed as a bundle.
The query uses explicit object, row, and timeout bounds with environment-backed credentials.
Aggregate evidence is preferred and unnecessary business values are not promoted into durable artifacts.

evals.prompt: The source exposes a native change feed with inserts, updates, and deletes but no usable watermark column in its base objects. Record discovery evidence without inventing a column candidate.
evals.expected_output: Use a source_native_change object outcome, describe observed coverage and limitations, and defer the final CDC/load selection to design.
expectations: Source-native change capability is represented without fabricating a watermark column.
Coverage and limitations remain explicit in the generated assessment table.
Discovery does not select final ingestion metadata or strategy.

evals.prompt: Rediscover only the ERP source in an existing project that also contains CRM observations. The new ERP probe is partial because several objects timed out. Show what changed without silently losing prior evidence.
evals.expected_output: Refresh an explicit source boundary into a scratch candidate, reject the partial replacement until ERP is explicitly accepted, preserve CRM byte-equivalent normalized rows, and generate a deterministic diff.
expectations: Refresh requires an exact base path, replacement source, and matching probe status.
Partial ERP evidence cannot replace the prior source without exact explicit acceptance.
Unselected CRM rows remain unchanged and added, removed, and changed ERP observations appear in a scratch diff.

evals.prompt: A source unsupported by packaged probes has a domain-specific column named RevClock that the owner says may track row changes. Capture the evidence without adding a special-case name to the skill or guessing missing facts.
evals.expected_output: Use bounded fallback inspection and owner evidence, leave unsupported facts empty, assess RevClock semantically, and validate manual observations through the canonical contract.
expectations: The workflow uses the generic fallback contract rather than modifying a global synonym list.
Unknown observation fields remain empty and source-level limitations are recorded in the report.
A confirmed role is applied only after bounded evidence or owner clarification and exact-key validation.

evals.prompt: Discover two incremental candidates. A mutable business object has no CDC or reliable change timestamp, but it has a filterable transaction_date and corrections normally arrive within five days. A file drop has no useful row timestamp, is stored under year/month/day/hour folders, and the platform exposes file modification times, though the owner has not confirmed whether restores preserve them.
evals.expected_output: Classify transaction_date only as a bounded backward fallback, inspect file delivery and path-layout semantics, and preserve framework virtual-column feasibility in the report without fabricating source-schema observations or choosing runtime metadata.
expectations: The transaction date is a backward fallback with correction horizon and older-correction risk, not claimed as complete change coverage.
File discovery verifies modification-time stability, rewrite or restore behavior, and actual ordered date-folder levels separately from row schema.
Framework virtual values are not fabricated in observations.csv and discovery leaves exact runtime metadata to build.
